task.title: Add a research note
task.shortdesc: Write down a question you are trying to answer, with a status, and tie it to the people it is about.

context.p: A research note is a question, an idea or a job to do. It has a status, such as open, in progress or resolved. This page adds the question of Patrick Brontë's surname.

stepresult.p: The page lists your research notes. Each shows its first words, its status and how many records it is linked from.

step.cmd: Choose , then choose in the part named , then choose .

info.p: The list scrolls. Turn the mouse wheel with the pointer on it to find the part.
This box is needed. For example, Question: what was Patrick's surname at birth, and when did he become Brontë? The sources give Brunty and Prunty. Still open: look for the parish register.

stepresult.p: A window named opens, with a box for a name.

step.cmd: Type Patrick Brontë, then choose the line with his years, 1777–1861, then choose .

info.p: The tree has more than one Patrick. The years show which one is which.

stepresult.p: The page lists the note by its first words. Under them it says Open · linked from 1 record(s).

result.p: The question is in your research log, tied to Patrick. Each note in the list has , and .
result.note: Good practice: write the question down before you start to answer it. A question can stay open until you find the evidence.
